subject.title: Feature: Streaming TTS pipeline for voice calls (sentence-level LLM→TTS→audio)

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a provider-generic classic Voice Call streaming-speech contract, and if so which initial carrier and TTS provider define its compatibility and cancellation semantics?
rationale: The existing mainline improvement deliberately delivers a completed early block, while the requested feature would add a cross-provider asynchronous speech contract and decide how Twilio, Telnyx, fallback, ordering, and barge-in behave.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded streaming contract
options.body: Define an additive async telephony-audio capability, implement and prove it first for Twilio plus one provider, then expand only after the queue and abort semantics are stable.

options.title: Keep early-block delivery as the supported latency path
options.body: Retain the current onBlockReply-to-TTS improvement and defer sentence-level streaming until a carrier-neutral contract has an owner and acceptance criteria.

options.title: Prefer realtime voice for new low-latency calls
options.body: Document realtime mode as the supported low-latency option while leaving the classic pipeline buffered apart from its existing early-block optimization.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded streaming contract
recommendation.body: Define an additive async telephony-audio capability, implement and prove it first for Twilio plus one provider, then expand only after the queue and abort semantics are stable.

likelyOwner.reason: Current mainline voice-call changes and the relevant early-TTS merge history route the design decision most directly to this area owner.
